subject: maths
question: A regular right pyramid with an equilateral triangular base of side 18 cm is completely submerged in a cylindrical tank of radius 10 cm, initially filled with water to a height of 25 cm. The pyramid's apex just touches the bottom of the tank. Given that the water level in the tank rises to 28 cm after the pyramid is submerged, find the perpendicular height of the pyramid.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume of water displaced = Volume of the submerged pyramid.

Rise in water level (h) = 28 − 25 = 3 cm.

Volume of cylinder (rise) = π × r² × h = 3.14 × 10² × 3 = 942 cm³.

Volume of pyramid = (1/3) × Base Area × Height = 942.

Base Area (Equilateral Triangle) = (√3/4) × 18² ≈ 0.433 × 324 ≈ 140.3 cm².

Height = (942 × 3) ÷ 140.3 ≈ 20.14 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 20.14 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of equilateral triangular base (a) = 18 cm

Radius of cylindrical tank (R) = 10 cm

Initial water height (H₁) = 25 cm

Final water height (H₂) = 28 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Cylinder = πR
